abstract.p: A compact printer system consists of at least a printer module and a range of further modules. The modules are connectable together to form a rod-shaped printer system. Each module has a connection means at one or both ends for interconnection of the modules. The connection means include a physical connection means and logical connection means. The physical connection means comprises a plug on a male connection means and a socket on a corresponding female connection means. The logical connection means comprises a serial bus. The serial bus consists of four conductive strips that carry power and data between modules.

L'invention concerne un système d'imprimante compacte qui consiste en au moins un module d'impression et une série d'autres modules. Les modules peuvent être connectés les uns aux autres pour former un système d'imprimante en forme de tige. Chaque module comporte un organe de connexion à au moins une de ses extrémités destiné à interconnecter les modules. Les organes de connexion comprennent des organes de connexion physique et logique. Les organes de connexion physique comprennent un tampon sur un organe de raccord mâle et un emboîtement sur un organe de raccord femelle correspondant. L'organe de connexion logique comprend un bus série. Le bus série comprend quatre bandes conductrices transportant l'énergie et les données entre les modules.

In the general case, the Pπnter Module holds the "current" image, and the other modules function with respect to this central repository of the current image. The Pπnter Module is therefore the central location for image interchange in the compact pπnter system, and the Pπnter Module provides a service to other modules as specified by user interaction. A given module may act as an image source. It therefore has the ability to transfer an image to the Printer

Module. A different module may act as an image store. It therefore has the ability to read the image from the Printer Module. Some modules act as both image store and image source These modules can both read images from and wπte images to the Pπnter Module's current image.

The standard image type has a single conceptual definition. The image definition is deπved from the physical attπbutes of the pπnthead used in the Pπnter Module. The pπnthead is 2 inches wide and pπnts at 1600dpi in cyan. magenta and yellow bi-level dots. Consequently a pπnted image from the compact pπnter system is 3200 bi-level dots wide.

The compact pπnter system pπnts on business card sized pages (85mm x 55mm). Since the pπnthead is 2 inches wide, the business cards are pπnted such that I line of dots is 2 inches. 2 inches is 50.8mm. leaving a 2mm edge on a standard business-card sized page. The length of the image is deπved from the same card size with a 2mm edge.
Consequently the pπnted image length is 81 mm. which equals 5100 1600dpi dots. The pπnted area of a page is therefore 81mm x 51mm. or 5100 x 3200 dots.

To obtain an integral contone to bi-level ratio a contone resolution of 267 ppi (pixels per inch) is chosen. This yields a contone CMY page size of 850 x 534. and a contone to bi-level ratio of 1.6 in each dimension. This ratio of 1 :6 provides no percened loss of quality since the output image is bi-level.

The pπnthead pπnts dots in cyan, magenta, and yellow ink The final output to the pπnted page must therefore be in the gamut of the pπnthead and take the attπbutes of the inks into account It would at first seem reasonable to use the CMY color space to represent images. However, the pπnter's CMY color space does not have a linear response. This is definitely true of pigmented inks, and partially true for dye-based inks The mαividual color profile ot a particular device
unput and output) can vary considerably. Image capture devices (such as digital cameras) typically work in RGB (red green blue) color space, and each sensor will have its own color response charactcπsucs.

Consequently, to allow for accurate conversion, as well as to allow for future image sensors, inks, and pπnters. Lhe CIE L*a*b* color model (CIE. 1986. CIE 15.2 Coloπmetry : Technical Report (2I>J Edition). Commission Internationale De I'Eclairagej is used for the compact pπnter system. L*a*b* is well defined, perceptually linear, and is a superset of other traditional color spaces (such as CMY. RGB. and HSV)

The Pπnter Module must therefore be capable of converting L*a*b* images to the particular pecuhaπties of its CMY color space. However, since the compact pπnter system allows tor connectivity to PCs. it is quite reasonable to also allow highly accurate color matching between screen and pπnter to be performed on the PC However the pπnter dnver or PC program must output L*a*b*.
Each pixel of a compact pπnter image is therefore represented by 24 bits: 8 bits each of L*. a*, and b*. The total image size is heretore 1.361.700 bytes (850 x 534 x 3).

Each image processing module is able to access the image stored in the Pπnter Module. The access is either to read the image from the Pπnter Module, or to wπte a new image to the Pπnter Module. The communications protocol for image access to the Pπntcr Module provides a choice of internal image organization. Images can be accessed either as 850 x 534 or as 534 x 850. They can also be accessed in interleaved or planar format. When accessed as interleaved, each pixel in the image is read or wπtten as 24 bits: 8 bits each of L*. a*, b*. When accessed as planar, each of the color planes can be read or wπtten independently. The entire image of L* pixels, a* pixels or b* pixels can be read or wπtten at a time. Low Power The Universal Seπal Bus (USB) specification caters for the requirements of the compact pπnter system USB is well defined and is easily integrated into a hardware architecture

The compact pπnter Seπal Bus requires a medium speed for transfemng images While not the high speed required for video, a reasonable speed for image transmission is required Although the maximum speed on USB is 12 MBits/sec. the maximum effective data transfer rate is 8MBιts sec due to protocol overhead and transmission redundancy The time taken to transmit a complete image (850 x 534 L*a*b") is theretore 1 36 seconds (850x534x3x 8/8.000.000).

Attachment or detachment ol a module from the compact pπnter system does not adversely affect the module or the rest of the system This is beneficial from an ease-of-use standpoint Users of the compact pπnter can attach modules and detach modules to reconfigure the system There is no need for individual on/off switches per module or special attachment procedures The compact pπnter modules are self identifying, and self configuπng (including bus termination). Users do not need to know anything about the electπcal system Users may simply connect the appropπate modules together and the compact pπnter system configures itself appropπately

Any given compact pπnter configuration consists of a number of compact pπnter modules connected to one another The exact number of compact pπnter modules depends on the requirements of the user In addition, the complete set of compact pπnter modules is not fixed The compact pπnter seπal bus allows new compact pπnter modules to be easily designed and added to the compact pπnter family USB allows up to 127 physical devices to be connected at a given time (power requirements not withstanding) Since the devices are self identifying, new modules can be added to a compact pπnter system as long as they coπtorm to the compact pπnter seπal protocol

The USB protocol is well-defined, this reduces design time, allows the use of pre-compiled cores, debugged protocols, and gives a large range of choice in terms of components The choice of USB also allows the compact pnnter system to be easily integrated into a PC environment for image download and upload

As descπbcd above, the pπnter module runs directly off an unregulated 3 V power supply (a 3 V battery). The compact pnnter Seπal Bus also runs off this power USB nominally runs at 5V Under normal circumstances, voltage at a powered hub-port must be no less than 4 75Vdc. while voltage at a bus-powered hub must be no less than 440Vdc. However this is the case for a completely open system (which the compact pπnter system is not) Consequently the USB used within compact pπnter modules can be lower power, and therefore run off an unregulated 3V power supply. This is the only difference between regular USB and USB as used in compact pπnter

There is no on/off switch on the compact pπnter Communication Module. The operating power is obtained from the computer's port power supply rather than the compact pπnter system power supply

Once physically connected, the logical mode of operation comes into play The ASIC in the compact pnnter Communication Module translates the compact pπnter modules into a virtual file system. Each compact pπnter module appears as a named sub-directory, each containing a set of numbered image files.
